item.title: Platonic geodesic trees in the $K-$Space
item.description: arXiv:2610.13950v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, We prove that: (A) If $m\ge 4,$ there exists a Platonic geodesic tree having $m$ edges (geodesic segments), which form $m$ platonic angles with measure $120^{o}$ and $(\frac{m(m-1)}{2}-m)$ platonic angles with measure $90^{o}.$ (Existence of a Fermat Coordinate system) (B) If $m=2,$ there exists a Platonic geodesic tree with three vertices and 2 edges, which meet at $120^{\circ}$ or $150^{\circ}$ or $180^{\circ}$ (Minimal spanning geodesic tree). (C) If $m=3,$ there exists a Platonic tree and the Steiner point is identical with the Fermat point, having three edges, which meet at $120^{\circ}$ (Hexagonal coordinate system). (D) If $m$ is even and $m \ge 4,$ there exists a Platonic geodesic tree having $m$ edges , which form platonic angles with only two distinct measures $90^{o}$ and $180^{\circ}.$ (Existence of a Cartesian coordinate system). (E) If $m\ge 4$, there does not exist a Platonic geodesic tree having $m$ edges , which form only platonic angles with measure $120^{o}$ (Non existence of a Fermat coordinate system). (F) If $m\ge 3,$ there does not exist a Platonic geodesic tree having $m$ edges, which form platonic angles with only one measure $150^{o},$ or two distinct measures $120^{\circ}$ and $150^{\circ}$ or two distinct measures $90^{\circ}$ and $150^{\circ}$ (Non existence of a Fermat coordinate system). A classification of platonic geodesic trees with boundary vertex set $V$ and added vertex set $Q$ in the $K-$Space is given by conditions (A), (B), (C), (D), (E), (F), which characterize each vertex in $V\cup Q.$
item.dc:creator: Anastasios N. Zachos

item.title: Breaking the Fourth Wall: The Planar Centroid Banach--Mazur Diameter Is Strictly Less than $4$
item.description: arXiv:2610.13952v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that the centroid Banach--Mazur diameter of planar convex bodies is strictly less than $4$, (slightly) improving the prior upper bound $69/17\approx 4.05882$ due to Lassak. The proof combines a sharp covariance-ellipse sandwich, whose equality cases in any single direction occur only for triangles, with a compactness argument: an extremal pair at distance $4$ would consist of two triangles, which are linearly equivalent and hence must in fact be at distance $1$. The resulting gap below $4$ is uniform but nonquantitative.
item.dc:creator: Scott Duke Kominers

item.title: On the Reverse Projection Inequality
item.description: arXiv:2610.13953v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In \cite {ChenFengLiXiXu2026}, a reverse projection inequality for general convex bodies was established in three dimensions. In this paper, we completely characterize the equality cases of this inequality. We further show that the reverse projection inequality fails in every dimension $n\geq9$. The counterexamples are constructed as full-dimensional polytopes with at most $n+2$ facets.
item.dc:creator: Yibin Feng, Shengnan Hu, Weiru Liu, Lei Xu

item.title: Certified Geometry and Admissible Motion of Gerver's Sofa
item.description: arXiv:2610.13955v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The moving sofa problem asks for the largest planar set that can pass through a unit-width right-angled hallway. Gerver's 1992 construction remains the largest explicit example, but its defining switching parameters, continuum of supporting hallways, and contact topology involve transcendental equations and global inequalities. We give a reproducible exact-rational certification of the construction. A strict four-dimensional Krawczyk inclusion encloses the reduced switching system, while an independent twenty-two-dimensional Krawczyk calculation verifies Romik's full matching and contact equations in an explicit rational box. Exact interval propagation through the five analytic phases proves the support identities, global half-plane constraints, inner-wall separation, niche topology, oriented contacts, injectivity, and area bounds. From the certified support functions we identify every supporting hallway as L_t=x(t)+R_tL. For G=K_0\setminus\mathcal N(K_0) we prove directly that G is nonempty, closed, and connected and that \Phi_t(q)=R_{-t}(q-x(t)) is a continuous path in SE(2) carrying G through the hallway, with the correct initial and final arms. We further identify G with Romik's reconstruction of Gerver's classical eighteen-piece sofa. The deterministic companion verifier uses only Python's standard library and exact rational arithmetic. As a consequence, the Gerver-specific geometric hypotheses in Baek's recent variational framework are rigorously certified; we also clarify the one-sided tangent-speed convention at two contact-curve junctions.
item.dc:creator: Dawid Trela

item.title: $L_p$-Integral Affine Surface Area-Variational Capacity Inequalities
item.description: arXiv:2610.13957v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For $n\geq 2$ and $1<p<n$, Ludwig-Xiao-Zhang \cite{LXYZ} asked whether the $L_p$-integral affine surface area of every convex body containing the origin in its interior is bounded above by the ball-normalized multiple of \(L_p\)-variational capacity, and whether the analogous analytic inequality holds for $L_p$-convexified level sets. We answer both questions negatively.
item.dc:creator: Yibin Feng, Ding Zhang

item.title: Thirteen Results in Magnitude Theory
item.description: arXiv:2610.13958v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove thirteen results concerning three aspects of magnitude theory. The first four concern small-scale magnitude and microscopic weightings. We identify the derivative of the magnitude function at the origin with maximal energy, allowing the value $+\infty$, and construct finite spaces for which small-scale magnitude diverges or for which the one-point property and finite concentration do not produce a microscopic weighting. A fifth result disproves the conjectured monotonicity of magnitude by giving a fourteen-point metric space of strict negative type whose magnitude function decreases. The remaining eight results concern continuity and dimension. Magnitude is Hausdorff-continuous at finite subsets of finite-dimensional positive definite normed spaces, but need not be continuous on compact subsets, even under convexity, geodesicity, bounded tractability, or simultaneous Hausdorff and Lipschitz convergence. The same constructions disprove an $\ell_1$-intrinsic-volume formula and two tractability conjectures. Finally, we construct a countable compact space of negative type whose Minkowski dimension is zero and whose lower and upper magnitude dimensions are both infinite.
item.dc:creator: Venkata Siddharth Pendyala

item.title: Necessary and Sufficient Criteria for the Realizability of Kaleidocycles Composed of Six Congruent Isosceles Tetrahedra
item.description: arXiv:2610.13961v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A classical kaleidocycle is a closed cyclic chain of congruent, edge-hinged tetrahedra with successive hinge axes at right angles, capable of continuous inside-out motion. Kaleidocycles composed of six isosceles tetrahedra (disphenoids) form a natural generalization in which consecutive hinge axes need not be perpendicular. Their kinematics are governed by the closure equation for threefold-symmetric Bricard 6R linkages. We derive a new compact closure equation directly from threefold symmetry using the composition of rotations, and show its equivalence to the classical formulation. Furthermore, we establish two equivalent necessary and sufficient criteria for a kaleidocycle to admit continuous, unblocked motion in terms of the geometric parameters of the constituent disphenoid. These criteria yield sharp bounds on the admissible geometric parameters of realizable kaleidocycles. Finally, we study assemblies of eight such kaleidocycles joined face-to-face. We identify a configuration exhibiting full octahedral symmetry, which forms a polyhedral structure closely related to the disdyakis dodecahedron.
item.dc:creator: Herbert Kociemba

item.title: A Power-Diagram Upper Bound for Twenty-Six Variable-Radius Disks in a Square
item.description: arXiv:2610.13962v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $S_{26}$ denote the supremum of the sum of the radii of 26 pairwise interior-disjoint closed disks of positive radius contained in the unit square. We prove $2.635983084917607783\ldots \le S_{26}\le \sqrt{\frac{2577}{2500}+\frac{11}{\sqrt3}}=2.716919756099889566\ldots$. The lower bound is accompanied by an exact rational feasibility certificate. For the upper bound, we assign the disks their clipped power cells, convert cell area into a reciprocal exterior-angle cost, and combine this local inequality with Euler side counts. The extremal case for the resulting relaxation has four boundary transitions and a four-cell boundary cycle; its continuous angle allocation is reduced to a concave one-variable problem. All finite numerical inequalities are rigorously enclosed by a reproducible certificate. The argument does not determine $S_{26}$ exactly, but gives a nontrivial global upper bound for a benchmark whose best-known packing is asymmetric.
item.dc:creator: Ayush Agarwal

item.title: A 0.41275 lower bound for the three-dimensional Blaschke-Lebesgue problem
item.description: arXiv:2610.13964v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that every convex body $K\subset\mathbb{R}^3$ of constant width $w>0$ satisfies \[ \operatorname{Vol}(K)\ge \frac{1651}{4000}w^3=0.41275\,w^3. \] This improves the certified lower bound $0.411040473721188\ldots\,w^3$ announced by Hyra and the earlier spectral bound $4\pi w^3/33$ of Nishioka. The main new ingredient is a contact-tetrahedron estimate near equality in Jung's circumradius inequality. Four balanced contacts of a minimum circumscribed ball form a near-regular tetrahedron; constant width then forces, beyond the tetrahedron itself, spherical regions over its faces, spindle sectors along its edges, and additional face-edge sectors. These regions can be selected with pairwise disjoint interiors and quantified by the total squared-edge deficit. A sharp convexity argument relates that deficit to the circumradius, and a symmetrization argument controls the four face contributions with only quadratic loss. This gives the analytic bound $\operatorname{Vol}(K)>0.41275318$ near the Jung endpoint. For the complementary circumradius range we use Hyra's radial transport/tangent-majorant mechanism together with closed-form contact and antipodal profiles. The antipodal contribution has an elementary primitive. For the contact contribution, a second-order concavity estimate converts the angular Jacobian into an explicit rational lower density; that density is monotone in the circumradius. The whole intermediate range therefore reduces to a single endpoint calculation, giving $\operatorname{Vol}(K)>0.41275168$. For smaller circumradius the tangent-majorant inequality with its nonnegative gap discarded already gives $\operatorname{Vol}(K)>0.41308109$. The proof is entirely analytic and requires no computer-assisted certificate.
item.dc:creator: Yunjiang Jiang

item.title: Jensen's inequality on parity classes of jump M-convex functions
item.description: arXiv:2610.13965v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove Jensen's inequality on each coordinatewise parity class of a jump $M$-convex function on $\mathbb{Z}^n$, without assuming strong base orderability or a finite effective domain. If a finite convex combination of domain points has its barycenter in the same parity class, then the barycenter belongs to the domain and satisfies Jensen's inequality. We also prove that every domain point admits an affine support on its entire parity class. The set of support vectors is characterized by at most $3^n-1$ local inequalities, which yield optimality certificates, attained duality, and an exact formula for linear growth and stability under linear perturbations. The same conclusions hold for distributions with finite first moment supported on domain points of a single parity class, provided their mean lies in that class. We characterize equality by contact sets and give a quantitative bound on the Jensen gap. The proof combines induction on dimension with the known closure under infimal convolution: convolution with an even-box indicator gives finite-domain supports, a quadratic kernel proves barycenter feasibility, and a fixed local kernel yields global supports. A two-dimensional example shows that total parity alone does not suffice.
item.dc:creator: Xinyue Liu

item.title: Insertion and expansion of cylinders around the unit ball
item.description: arXiv:2610.13972v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Surround a unit ball with a ring of $n$ equal infinite circular cylinders, each touching the ball and its two neighbors. Can one more such cylinder be added, for a total of $n+1$, if we are allowed to rearrange the configuration? We prove that the answer is ``no'' for $3\le n\le 7$, and ``yes'' if $n\geq 9$. The case $n=8$ remains open. The case $n=6$, where the cylinders are the same size as the ball, is Kuperberg's problem from 1990, resolved recently. We also make progress on a conjecture of Ogievetsky and Shlosman, confirming the first decimal digit of their predicted value for the largest radius of four non-overlapping cylinders that touch a ball.
item.dc:creator: Ivan Mati\'c, Rado\v{s} Radoi\v{c}i\'c, Andreas Spomer

item.title: The rhombic dodecahedral conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2610.13975v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that every three-dimensional parallelohedron $P$ satisfies \[ \mathcal H^2(\partial P)\ge 12\sqrt2\,r(P)^2, \] where $r(P)$ is the inradius of $P$, with equality if and only if $P$ is similar to the regular rhombic dodecahedron.
item.dc:creator: Annalisa Cesaroni, Matteo Novaga

item.title: An Improved Lower Bound for Packing 203 Equal Spheres in a Unit Cube
item.description: arXiv:2610.13978v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper reports an improved numerical lower bound for packing 203 equal spheres in a unit cube. Let r denote the maximum common radius of equal non-overlapping spheres that can be packed in a unit cube. For N = 203, the configuration currently listed in Packomania has a feasible radius of approximately r = 0.088145402159. Starting from this public configuration, we perform further numerical optimization and obtain a new feasible configuration with r > 0.088145634693. The final configuration is checked by an independent verification program using 100-digit arithmetic. All 20503 sphere-pair constrains and all 1218 sphere-wall constraints are satisfied. The coordinates of the new configuration and the related programs are provided as supplementary material.
item.dc:creator: Peng Lu

item.title: Equilateral sets in $\ell_p^n$ beyond $n+1$: Linear excess and dimension cost
item.description: arXiv:2610.13983v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: How many equilateral points can $\ell_p^n$ contain beyond $n+1$? For every fixed real $p>4$, we construct equilateral sets for which the number of points beyond $n+1$ grows at least linearly with $n$. For every fixed dimension, we prove that the maximum is $n+1$ at all sufficiently large finite $p$, with an explicit threshold. The least dimension admitting any fixed number of extra points is $p^{1+o(1)}$ as $p\to\infty$. The constructions and finite bounds are formalised in Lean. Thus $p=4$ marks the boundary: $n+1$ is exact in every dimension for $2\leq p\leq4$, while at every fixed finite $p>4$ the excess grows at least linearly with dimension.
item.dc:creator: Logan R. Chalmers, Aran S. Ziegler

item.title: Polygons and coplanar points on submanifolds of codimension 2
item.description: arXiv:2610.14032v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Problem 73 on Green's list of open problems asks whether a smooth submanifold of codimension two in $\mathbb{R}^n$ must meet some affine two-plane in five points when $n$ is large. In this paper, we answer this question for every $n \geq 6$. Every nonempty relatively open subset of such a submanifold contains the vertices of an affinely regular pentagon, and the bound $n \geq 6$ is sharp for affinely regular pentagons. More generally, for every prime $p \geq 5$, the graph of a continuous map from a ball in $\mathbb{R}^{p-1}$ to $\mathbb{R}^2$ contains an affinely regular $p$-gon. A second argument gives six coplanar points when $n \geq 7$. Both proofs find the points by making the low Fourier modes of the graph map vanish along a circle.
item.dc:creator: Sohail (Neel), Sarkar

item.title: Sharp Antipode-Neighbor Bounds in Every Dimension
item.description: arXiv:2610.14037v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $P\subset\mathbb R^d$ be finite with $\operatorname{diam}(P)\le1$. For $0<\varepsilon<1$, let $\mathcal N_\varepsilon(P)$ denote the number of ordered pairs at distance at most $\varepsilon$, including the diagonal, and let $\mathcal A_\varepsilon(P)$ denote the number of ordered pairs at distance at least $1-\varepsilon$. We prove the sharp bound \[ \mathcal N_\varepsilon(P)\gtrsim_d \varepsilon^{(d-1)/2}\mathcal A_\varepsilon(P) \] conjectured by Steinerberger (2025). More generally, the same inequality holds for finite positive Borel measures. The main input is a uniform $L^2$ estimate, at cap thickness comparable to lattice spacing, for a supporting-direction incidence operator. In gnomonic coordinates, this operator is controlled by an incidence estimate for small Fenchel--Young gaps.
item.dc:creator: Samuel Korsky

item.title: Maximal volumes of pyramids in the unit cube
item.description: arXiv:2610.14047v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $Q_n=[0,1]^n$, $n\ge2$. Denote by $M_n$ be the maximal volume of a pyramid in $Q_n$ whose base is a hyperplane section of $Q_n$, and by $M_n^0$ the corresponding maximum when the section contains the center of $Q_n$. We prove that $nM_n<(n+1)M_{n+1}^0$.
item.dc:creator: Nikolai Nikolov

item.title: Upper bounds for Jung constants of $\ell_1^d$
item.description: arXiv:2610.14055v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For every integer $k\ge1$, we prove that each nonempty bounded set in real $\ell_1^{4k+1}$ has an ambient enclosing ball of radius at most $(4k-1)/(4k)$ times its diameter. The bound is sharp in dimension five: $J(\ell_1^5)=3/4$. If a Hadamard matrix of order $4k$ exists, then $J(\ell_1^{4k-1})=J(\ell_1^{4k})=J(\ell_1^{4k+1})=(4k-1)/(4k)$. The upper bound for every $k\ge1$ has been formalized in Lean.
item.dc:creator: Xiao Li

item.title: Quasiconformal uniformization and extension for planar trees
item.description: arXiv:2610.14236v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A classical uniformization theorem of Ahlfors from 1963 asserts that every bounded turning planar arc is the image of the unit segment under a quasiconformal self-map of the plane. We prove an analogous uniformization theorem for planar trees by showing that every planar quasiconformal tree with uniform branch separation is quasiconformally equivalent to a quasiconvex planar tree with uniform branch separation and Hausdorff dimension arbitrarily close to 1. Along the way, we show that every quasisymmetric (resp. bi-Lipschitz) homeomorphism between planar quasiconformal trees that respects the counterclockwise orientation of the branches at every branch point can be extended quasisymmetrically (resp. bi-Lipscitz) to the whole plane. As a corollary of the extension theorem we construct a large class of quadrivalent quasiconformal trees, which includes the Vicsek fractal, so that each tree in this class is the Julia set of a uniformly quasiregular map of $\mathbb{R}^2$.
item.dc:creator: Fotis Ioannidis Vyron Vellis

item.title: Lattices with Large Kissing Number from Local Density
item.description: arXiv:2610.14380v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $\kappa_p(n)$ denote the maximum kissing number of a lattice $\mathcal{L} \subset \mathbb{R}^n$. We prove that $\kappa_p(n) \geq 2^{\Omega(\sqrt{n})}$ for all $p\ge 1$ and that $\kappa_p(n) \geq \Omega(\alpha_p^n)$ for all $p > 2$, where $\alpha_p > 1$ is a constant depending only on $p$. In particular, our former result improves on the previously best known lower bound of $\kappa_2(n) \geq 2^{\Theta(\log^2 n)}$ for the $\ell_2$ kissing number, which has stood for over $60$ years. (In concurrent and independent work, Laarhoven and Kominers [arXiv, 2026] showed a similar lower bound on $\kappa_2(n)$ using similar techniques.) In fact, our lower bounds follow from efficient (randomized) constructions of lattices with large kissing number. Our results use a general construction of lattices with large kissing number. Specifically, we show a simple equivalence between such lattices and a new object that we call an exact locally dense lattice. Closely related objects appear throughout the literature on computational lattice problems. Our constructions of lattices with large kissing number then follow as corollaries by showing that constructions due to Bennett and Peikert [RANDOM, 2023] (using Craig lattices) and Aggarwal and Stephens-Davidowitz [STOC, 2018] (using sparsification of $\mathbb{Z}^n$) in fact give exact locally dense lattices, as well as a new construction of exact locally dense lattices built from rotations of the $m$-dimensional checkerboard lattice $D_m$.
item.dc:creator: Huck Bennett, Minki Hhan, Zihan Li, Noah Stephens-Davidowitz

item.title: Unrectifiable surfaces with intrinsic regularity in Carnot groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.15851v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In any noncommutative Carnot group, for every $0\le \alpha<1$, we show the existence of a $C^{1,\alpha}_\mathrm H$ surface that is unrectifiable with respect to the Euclidean distance. Precisely, the surface has Euclidean Hausdorff dimension higher than its topological dimension. We show that in step-2 Carnot groups the construction gives hypersurfaces of maximal Euclidean Hausdorff dimension, equal to $q-\frac{1+\alpha}{2}$, where $q$ is the topological dimension of the group. Here the range of unrectifiability is sharp, since for $\alpha=1$ the surface is rectifiable in the classical sense. In step-2 Carnot groups, it is also possible to prove that the $(q-\frac12)$-dimensional Euclidean Hausdorff measure of every $C^1_\mathrm H$ hypersurface is zero. These results extend the seminal work by Kirchheim and Serra Cassano in the first Heisenberg group.
item.dc:creator: Valentino Magnani, Jeremy Mirmina

item.title: Exponential profiles for the intrinsic volumes of Orlicz balls
item.description: arXiv:2610.16904v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: An Orlicz ball is the set of points where the sum of a fixed even convex function of the coordinates does not exceed a given radius, here proportional to the dimension. For a broad class of such functions, including non-homogeneous ones, we find the exponential rate of the intrinsic volumes whose order is proportional to the dimension and express it by a two-parameter variational formula involving only one-dimensional integrals. As a function of the order-to-dimension ratio, this rate is concave and continuous on the closed unit interval, and the convergence is uniform in the order. This proves the exponential-profile conjecture of Kabluchko, Marynych, and Prochno for these bodies and recovers their result for $\ell_p$ balls with $p>1$. The proof relies on the theory of large deviations. An exact formula for the Laplace transform of the intrinsic volumes in the radius, extending theirs for $\ell_p$ balls, plays the role of a moment generating function, and a Laplace method gives its exponential rate. An exponential change of measure, analogous to that used in Cram\'{e}r's theorem, then recovers the intrinsic volumes. The key step is a lower bound on the tilted density at its mean, obtained from log-concavity rather than a law of large numbers.
item.dc:creator: Mykyta Sadok

item.title: A new family of constant width bodies obtained from Reuleaux polyhedra
item.description: arXiv:2610.16997v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give a construction of a body of constant width from a unit Reuleaux polyhedron that preserves all its symmetries. As opposed to the Meissner surgery, our construction modifies both edges of each dual pair and requires no choice between them. For the Reuleaux tetrahedron it recovers a previously known body of constant width with six elliptic edges and tetrahedral symmetry.
item.dc:creator: Marcela G. Mercado-Flores, Edgardo Rold\'an-Pensado

item.title: Intrinsic Rigidity of Bar-and-Joint Frameworks on Riemannian Manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2610.17004v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop an intrinsic rigidity theory for bar-and-joint frameworks whose vertices are constrained to a Riemannian manifold and whose edges are given by minimizing geodesic arcs. Such frameworks are called rigid if they cannot be deformed beyond the ambient isometries, while preserving the geodesic edge lengths. For admissible placements, for which adjacent vertices are joined by unique minimizing geodesics, we define a coordinate-free rigidity operator as the differential of the squared geodesic distance of the edges. By the first-variation formula, its edge rows are expressed in terms of the Riemannian logarithm, providing an intrinsic analogue of the classical Euclidean rigidity matrix. Trivial motions are characterized by orbits of the diagonal action of the isometry group, leading to notions of infinitesimal and local rigidity. We further develop a covariant second-order rigidity theory using the Riemannian Hessians of the edge constraints and characterize second-order rigidity through self-stresses and associated quadratic forms. Finally, we show that infinitesimal and second-order rigidity can be used as sufficient conditions for the local rigidity of an intrinsic framework. Our overarching goal is to provide a unified differential-geometric formulation of intrinsic framework rigidity on smooth manifolds.
item.dc:creator: Matthias Adrian-Himmelmann

item.title: Steiner Minimal Trees in the Gromov--Hausdorff Space and in Gromov--Hausdorff Clouds
item.description: arXiv:2610.17400v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove the existence of Steiner minimal trees spanning a finite family of metric spaces in two cases of the Gromov--Hausdorff theory. In the compact Gromov--Hausdorff space $\mathcal{M}$, every finite family of nonempty compact metric spaces is spanned by a shortest Steiner minimal tree whose Steiner vertices are again nonempty compact metric spaces. In a fixed Gromov--Hausdorff cloud $\mathcal{C}$, every finite family of proper, isometrically cobounded spaces admits a finite-length Steiner minimal tree all of whose vertices remain in $\mathcal{C}$. The compact case uses compact replacement through distance profiles and the Hausdorff hyperspace, and the cloud case uses pointed ultralimits.
item.dc:creator: I. N. Mikhailov

item.title: Non-smooth sub-Riemannian manifolds with non-integer dimension and a Poincar\'e inequality
item.description: arXiv:2610.17863v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For every integer $d\geq 3$ and real number $Q\in \left(d,\frac{d(d-1)+2}{2}\right]$, we construct a $Q$-Ahlfors regular metric measure manifold $(M,\mathbf{d},\mu)$ of topological dimension $d$ and analytic dimension $2$ that satisfies a Poincar\'e inequality. For every $Q>\frac{d(d-1)+2}{2}$, the construction yields a metric measure manifold $(M,\mathbf{d},\mu)$ that is doubling, satisfies a Poincar\'e inequality, and for which $M$ has $\mu$-essential Hausdorff dimension $Q$. The manifold is $\mathbb{R}^d$ equipped with Lebesgue measure and a sub-Riemannian distance given by vector fields that are locally H\"older continuous but not Lipschitz continuous. These metrics give an uncountable family of new models that are genuinely distinct from the only known families of metric manifolds satisfying a Poincar\'e inequality: weighted and deformed Carnot groups and smooth sub-Riemannian spaces. The construction is modeled on a singular variant of a filiform Carnot group.
item.dc:creator: Sylvester Eriksson-Bique, Enrico Le Donne

item.title: Geometry and barycenters in large $\CAT(\kappa)$ spaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.17909v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the geometry and resulting properties of Fr\'echet functions and barycenters in metric spaces with curvature bounded above by a positive constant in the sense of Alexandrov. Existing results typically rely on the assumption that the support is small enough that the squared distance, and thus the Fr\'echet function, is strongly geodesically convex. We work in the sharper regime where existence and uniqueness of the barycenter are guaranteed, but where convexity typically fails. We develop new geometric properties of these spaces, including a quantitative four-point inequality and a geodesic stability result. Using these tools, we establish new finite sample error bounds for two statistical estimators: the empirical barycenter and the iterated barycenter, as well as new results on sparse representations and approximations of barycenters.
item.dc:creator: Yassine Boukhateb, Victor-Emmanuel Brunel, Austin J. Stromme

item.title: Excess inertia of finite metric spaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.18132v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper classifies the possible inertias that are realized by an excess matrix of a finite metric space with at most nine points. For the classification, we make use of relationships between finite metric spaces and non-obtuse and acute sets in classical geometry. As an application, we prove that the small-scale limit of the magnitude function of any six-point metric space is at least one whenever this limit exists.
item.dc:creator: Kiyonori Gomi

item.title: Radon Transforms of Projection Functions and Aleksandrov-Fenchel Inequalities
item.description: arXiv:2610.18268v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Radon transforms on Grassmannians define two families of geometric operators on convex bodies when applied to their projection functions. On the one hand, these are Minkowski's projection body maps and on the other hand these operators coincide on origin-symmetric bodies with the mean section body maps introduced by Goodey and Weil in 1992. Over the past two decades various sharp isoperimetric inequalities for projection bodies were shown to also hold for mean section bodies. However, an analogue of Lutwak's log-concavity inequalities for the intrinsic volumes of projection bodies remained open for mean section bodies. We establish new Aleksandrov--Fenchel inequalities for averages of certain mixed volumes and apply them to show that also all the intrinsic volumes of mean section bodies are indeed log-concave.
item.dc:creator: Leo Brauner, Oscar Ortega-Moreno, Franz E. Schuster

item.title: An explicit dimension-free isoperimetric plateau in the cube
item.description: arXiv:2610.18351v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that, in every dimension, the relative Euclidean isoperimetric profile of the unit cube equals one whenever the prescribed volume differs from one half by at most $6.25\times10^{-12}$. The only minimizers in this interval are coordinate slabs. This answers Glaudo's question on the existence of a dimension-free central plateau. The proof combines a dimension-free local optimality estimate for slabs, established through BV slicing and a small-support estimate, with a quantitative Gaussian rigidity argument that forces the normal of an approximating half-space to be close to a coordinate direction.
item.dc:creator: Lei Yu

item.title: On plank coverings of cube annuli
item.description: arXiv:2610.18770v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study plank coverings of cube annuli $Q\setminus\delta Q\subset\mathbb{R}^d$, where $Q$ is the $d$-dimensional unit cube and $\delta Q$ is a homothetic copy lying in its interior. A. Bezdek proved that, in dimension $2$, every plank covering of such an annulus has total width at least~1 whenever $\delta\le1-1/\sqrt2$. Smurov, Bogataya, and Bogatyi extended this result to all $d\ge2$ under the condition $\delta\le1-1/\sqrt d$. It is conjectured that the same lower bound holds for $\delta\le1-1/d$. We provide evidence for this conjecture in dimensions $2$ and $3$ by proving that there exist positive constants $\varepsilon_2$ and $\varepsilon_3$ such that the bound remains valid whenever $\delta\le1-1/\sqrt d+\varepsilon_d$.
item.dc:creator: Gergely Ambrus, Matthew Corbo, Dakota Nobuyuki Goto, Desmond Leitz, Kai Mawhinney

item.title: Bisectors in the Heisenberg group II
item.description: arXiv:2610.13954v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Following previous work on metric bisectors with respect to the Kor\'anyi metric, we study here bisectors in the Heisenberg group $\mathfrak{H}$ equipped with the Carnot--Carath\'eodory metric $d_{cc}$.
item.dc:creator: Gaoshun Gou, Joonhyung Kim, Ioannis D. Platis, Li-Jie Sun

item.title: Triangles and quadrilaterals suffice
item.description: arXiv:2610.13986v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove a conjecture proposed by Robert J. Lang over 20 years ago, stating that in a circle-packed origami design, any axial polygon with 5 or more sides can be reduced by properly adding a new circle. The proof is based on the structure of the medial axis of the region enclosed by the circles, and yields a concrete algorithm for finding the added circle. The result extends to configurations involving rivers.
item.dc:creator: Mu-Tsun Tsai

item.title: An upper bound for the three-dimensional moving sofa problem in a snaky corridor
item.description: arXiv:2610.14050v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $K_M \subset \mathbb{R}^3$ be the "snaky" corridor with unit-square cross-section: an infinite entry arm parallel to the $x$-axis, a middle arm parallel to the $y$-axis whose clear straight section has length $M$, and an infinite exit arm parallel to the $z$-axis, with the two turns lying in the $x$-$y$ and $y$-$z$ planes. Let $V^*(K_M)$ be the supremum of the volumes of connected bodies that can be moved continuously (by rigid motions) from the entry arm to the exit arm while remaining inside $K_M$. We prove $V^*(K_M) \le 7.8691$ for every $M \ge 3.53$ (Theorem A); by a sharper analysis of the same mechanism, $V^*(K_M) \le 4.2862$ for every $M \ge 2.61$ (Theorem B); and, by replacing the final analytic caps with a certified branch-and-bound computation over the compact family of entry tubes compatible with the forced events, $V^*(K_M) \le 3.4083$ for every $M > 2.2$ (Theorem C; computer-assisted, in double precision with conservative slack). In particular all three bounds apply to the corridor with $M = 4$ used in Problem 6.64 of Georgiev, G\'omez-Serrano, Tao and Wagner (arXiv:2511.02864), and uniformly to every "turns far apart" reading of that problem. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first upper bound for the snaky-corridor 3D moving sofa problem; previously not even finiteness of $V^*$ had been recorded. This note proves upper bounds only; combined with the certified lower bound 1.8558404 from the author's separate certification work via the problem's own evaluation pipeline, the state of the problem becomes $1.8558404 \le V^*(K_4) \le 3.4083$. Theorems A and B are elementary and self-contained: a first-crossing (elbow) event forces a definite tilt of the body's own entry tube, and Fubini-type chord estimates for tilted tubes cap the volume. Theorem C certifies, by the same forced-event skeleton, the largest corridor volume that any admissible entry tube can carry.
item.dc:creator: Yuzhe Tang

item.title: New certified lower bounds for the moving sofa problem in a three-dimensional snaky corridor
item.description: arXiv:2610.14051v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Consider the "snaky" corridor $K_4 \subset \mathbb{R}^3$ from Problem 6.64 of arXiv:2511.02864: a tube of unit-square cross-section whose two right-angle turns lie in perpendicular planes, with a straight middle section of clear length $4$. We exhibit explicit rigid motions of connected bodies through $K_4$ and certify their volumes with the problem's own evaluation pipeline, unmodified, at the tight motion tolerances of its final scoring stage (translation $0.005$, rotation $0.05$ degrees). The certificates give $V^*(K_4) \ge 1.8355162$ at grid fineness $0.002$ and $V^*(K_4) \ge 1.8558404$ at grid fineness $0.001$, against the previously reported $1.81$; rerunning the pipeline's published best path under the identical configuration yields $1.8179428$, so every comparison is path against path under one fixed certifier. Three stages produce the record motion: a simple "staggered twist" backbone in which the whole 90-degree twist about the tube axis happens inside the second turn; evolutionary (CMA-ES) refinement, including a mixed-fidelity scheme that re-scores each generation's leading candidates on a grid twice as fine and lets those ranks steer recombination; and a gradient polish carried out directly at the finer carve resolution, guarded by periodic rebuilding of the frozen interpolation structure and by a penalty on control-pose spacing. These guards close three documented failure modes in which an optimizer inflates its own objective: frozen-structure inflation, spacing stretch, and exploitation of a coarse grid by optimizing and selecting on it. A staircase-based predictor with two grid bases, anchored by matching grid sensitivity, forecast the certificates to about $0.001$ before the runs. With the companion note's upper bound $V^*(K_4) \le 3.4083$, the problem now sits in the bracket $1.8558404 \le V^*(K_4) \le 3.4083$. All paths, notebooks and certified results are public.
item.dc:creator: Yuzhe Tang

item.title: Uniformly Bounded Orthonormal Bases of Homogeneous Polynomials on the Complex Sphere
item.description: arXiv:2610.14160v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We resolve the long-standing problem of Rudin concerning uniformly bounded orthonormal bases of homogeneous polynomials on complex unit spheres. Specifically, we show that for every $K \geq 2$ and $N \geq 0$ there exists a basis of degree $N$ homogeneous polynomials in $\mathbb{C}^K$ that is orthonormal with respect to the surface measure of the unit sphere of $\mathbb{C}^K$ and uniformly bounded by a constant depending only on $K$ on the unit ball of $\mathbb{C}^K$. Bourgain resolved the case $K = 2$ in 1985 and the case $K = 3$ in 2016. No cases $K \geq 4$ were previously known.
item.dc:creator: Felipe Gon\c{c}alves, Jo\~ao P. Ferreira, Maksym Radziwi\l{}\l{}

item.title: Polytopal invariance for Lusztig's $q$-weight multiplicities
item.description: arXiv:2610.14275v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $\Phi$ be an irreducible root system normalized so that long roots have length $\sqrt{2}$, and let $\mu\leq\lambda$ be dominant weights. We associate to $(\Phi,\mu,\lambda)$ the convex polytope $$P^{\Phi}_{\mu,\lambda} = (\mu+C)\cap(\lambda-C)\cap(\overline{D}-\rho),$$ where $C=\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}\Phi^+$ and $\overline{D}$ is the closed dominant Weyl chamber. We prove that if $P^{\Phi}_{\mu,\lambda}$ and $P^{\Phi'}_{\mu',\lambda'}$ are isometric, then $$K^{\Phi}_{\lambda\mu}(q)=K^{\Phi'}_{\lambda'\mu'}(q),$$ where $K^{\Phi}_{\lambda\mu}(q)$ is Lusztig's $q$-analogue of the $\mu$-weight multiplicity in the irreducible highest-weight representation $V(\lambda)$, often called the generalized Kostka-Foulkes polynomial. Moreover, we construct the polynomial directly from the metric shape of the polytope, and we classify when two such polytopes are isometric. Such coincidences are abundant and can occur in different Dynkin types, and in different Dynkin families. By the Lusztig-Kato theorem, the main theorem gives a metric analogue, in the spherical setting, of the combinatorial invariance conjecture for Kazhdan-Lusztig polynomials.
item.dc:creator: Nicol\'as Libedinsky

item.title: Asymptotics of Random-Lattice Enumeration: Beyond HKZ via Dense Sublattices
item.description: arXiv:2610.15265v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: To bridge the gap between worst-case and heuristic analyses of lattice enumeration, we study the sizes of (unpruned) enumeration trees on $n$-dimensional Haar-random lattices. Writing $n^{cn+o(n)}$ for the tree size at the shortest vector radius, we investigate the asymptotic scaling of $c$, and which bases minimize it. For quasi-HKZ bases, we rigorously analyze the random-lattice HKZ geometry and establish $c=1/(2e)\approx 0.1839$. This matches the worst-case enumeration exponent of Hanrot-Stehl\'{e} and confirms earlier predictions for the geometry of HKZ bases on random lattices. Searching beyond quasi-HKZ bases, we prove that with high probability, the minimum achievable tree size exponent $c$ over all bases of a random lattice satisfies: \begin{align} 0.1464 \approx \frac{2-\sqrt{2}}{4}\leq c<0.1474. \end{align} For the lower bound, we use Kim's mean-value formula for nested chains of primitive sublattices to rule out bases with small prefix determinants. This strengthens the earlier Rankin-based heuristic lower bound exponent $c \geq 1/8$, discussed by Nguyen and Hanrot-Stehl\'{e}, and rules out the existence of random-lattice bases with trees as small as predicted by the geometric series assumption. For the upper bound, we show that with high probability a dense primitive half-rank sublattice exists with determinant at most $n^{n/8 + o(n)}$. Combining dual HKZ on this sublattice with HKZ on its quotient gives a basis with $c \leq 1/(4\sqrt{e}) \approx 0.1516$. Recursively splitting each half lowers the upper bound below $0.1474$, and under a natural heuristic assumption we prove that the lower bound is tight. Combined with the collision search of Feng-Gao-Liu, our two-block construction gives a polynomial-space algorithm solving the closest vector problem with preprocessing (CVPP) on random lattices in query time $n^{0.0892 n + o(n)}$ for arbitrary targets.
item.dc:creator: Thijs Laarhoven

item.title: Every n points in the plane contain (m1 + o(1)) n points with no unit distance
item.description: arXiv:2610.15424v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $f(n)$ be the largest integer such that every set of $n$ points in the plane contains $f(n)$ points no two at distance $1$, and let $m_1$ be the supremum of the upper densities of Lebesgue measurable planar sets with no two points at distance $1$. Larman and Rogers observed that $f(n) \ge m_1 n$. We prove that $f(n)/n \to m_1$; that is, $f(n) = (m_1 + o(1))n$. This is the first half of a conjecture of D\'ucz and Varga, and with the bound $m_1 \le 0.247$ of Ambrus, Csisz\'arik, Matolcsi, Varga and Zs\'amboki it gives $f(n) \le (0.247 + o(1))n$. The proof builds a random independent subset of the algebraic plane, invariant under algebraic translations and rotations, whose probability of containing the origin is at least the worst finite independence ratio, and turns it into a measurable planar set of at least that upper density. Its only non-classical input is the Haar rigidity theorem for wild character laws from the OpenAI preprint The Euclidean plane is not five-colorable, which has a machine-checked Lean proof. The whole argument has been formalized in Lean 4 on top of it.
item.dc:creator: Shisheng Li, Yong Su

item.title: Sharp Rogers--Shephard Inequalities for R\'enyi Entropy
item.description: arXiv:2610.15716v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We establish sharp weighted Rogers--Shephard inequalities for R\'enyi differential entropy. For independent copies $X,X'$ of a log-concave random vector in $\R^n$, we prove $h_p(aX-bX')\le h_p(X)+n\log(a+b)$ for all $a,b>0$ and $1\le p\le\infty$, where orders $1$ and $\infty$ correspond to Shannon entropy and min-entropy, respectively. The Shannon case settles the entropic Rogers--Shephard conjecture of Madiman and Kontoyiannis and its higher-dimensional formulation. For $1\le p<\infty$, equality holds precisely for invertible affine images of random vectors with independent exponential coordinates. At $p=\infty$, the larger equality class is characterized by possibly extended-valued convex potentials that are positively homogeneous of degree one. For every $0<p<1$, uniform laws on sufficiently high-dimensional simplices violate the unweighted bound. Thus $p=1$ is the critical order for this bound to hold in every dimension. The proof combines weighted convex intersections with an exponential lift to a log-affine probability density. At the Shannon endpoint, this lift yields an exact deficit decomposition with a conditional mutual information term for an additive channel with asymmetric Laplace noise.
item.dc:creator: Bang-Xian Han, Guoqing Zhan, Chiyu Zhou, Zhuo-Nan Zhu

item.title: The $p$-Bures-Wasserstein distance via $3\times3$ block matrices (with application to $p$-Bures-Wasserstein barycenters)
item.description: arXiv:2610.15889v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the $p$-Bures-Wasserstein distance $D_p(A,B)=(\mathrm{tr}\,A^p+\mathrm{tr}\,B^p-2\|A^{1/2}B^{1/2}\|_p^p)^{1/2}$ on positive semidefinite matrices; it equals the Bures-Wasserstein distance for $p=1$, and the Hilbert-Schmidt distance for $p=2$. We prove that $D_p$ is a metric for every $1\le p\le2$, by proving a stronger 2014 conjecture of Lin and van den Driessche on $3\times3$ block matrices. Our main tool is a partition inequality for Schatten norms, proved by complex interpolation. We also characterize Fr\'echet means for $D_p$ by a fixed-point equation and prove geometric convergence of the associated iteration.
item.dc:creator: Suvrit Sra

item.title: Revisiting the Bobkov-Chistyakov-G\"otze theorem on approximately Gaussian marginals
item.description: arXiv:2610.16740v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study one-dimensional marginals of an isotropic, log-concave probability measure in $\mathbb{R}^n$. We show that the Kolmogorov distance between a typical marginal and the standard Gaussian distribution is at most $C/n$, for a universal constant $C > 0$. This bound is optimal in general, up to the value of the universal constant. It improves the Gaussian approximation bound of Bobkov, Chistyakov and G\"otze by a logarithmic factor in the log-concave setting.
item.dc:creator: Boaz Klartag

item.title: Absolutely minimising Lipschitz extensions between Hilbert spaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.17194v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Every Lipschitz map from a closed subset of a real Hilbert space into a real Hilbert space has an absolutely minimising Lipschitz extension: an extension whose Lipschitz constant on every open subset of the complement, bounded or not, equals the Lipschitz constant of its restriction to the boundary of that subset. Neither space need be separable. This answers a question of Naor and Sheffield. For targets of dimension at least two we prove a density theorem on connected domains: every optimal extension of a boundary datum can be approximated, uniformly on compact sets, by extensions whose Lipschitz constant on every nonempty open subset, and on its boundary, equals the constant of the datum. Consequently, in contrast with the scalar case, such a datum has a unique absolutely minimising extension exactly when its optimal extension is unique, and absolutely minimising extensions need not be closed under uniform convergence, even for fixed smooth data on a planar disk. The extensions are built by finite piecewise isometric interpolation: on nested polyhedra with dense union they are piecewise affine and preserve distances in at least two directions on each simplex, a structure described through leaves of 1-Lipschitz maps. The boundary constraints are handled by a midpoint argument for admissible values, and a Kuratowski-Zorn argument removes the separability assumption while preserving previously prescribed values. We also characterise the bounded linear maps that are absolutely minimising extensions of all data determining their operator norm.
item.dc:creator: Krzysztof J. Ciosmak

item.title: Integer decomposition property of three-dimensional smooth polytopes: a shorter proof
item.description: arXiv:2610.17270v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Oda's smoothness conjecture asserts that every smooth lattice polytope has the integer decomposition property. The three-dimensional case of this conjecture was recently proven by AI. Here we give a much shorter proof of this result.
item.dc:creator: Juliana Curtis, Gaku Liu

item.title: Multiple Lattice Packings and Coverings of the Plane with Triangles
item.description: arXiv:1412.5096v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Given a convex disk $K$ and a positive integer $j$, let $\delta_L^j(K)$ and $\vartheta_L^j(K)$ denote the $j$-fold lattice packing density and the $j$-fold lattice covering density of $K$, respectively. I will prove that for every triangle $T$ we have that $\delta_L^j(T)=\frac{2j^2}{2j+1}$ and $\vartheta_L^j(T)=\frac{2j+1}{2}$. Furthermore, I also obtain that the numbers of lattices which attain these densities both are $(2j+1)\prod_{p|2j+1}(1-\frac{2}{p})$, where the product is over the distinct prime numbers dividing $2j+1$.
item.dc:creator: Kirati Sriamorn

item.title: On the Structure of Busemann Spaces with Non-Negative Curvature I
item.description: arXiv:2508.12348v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We extend the structure theory of Burago--Gromov--Perelman for Alexandrov spaces with curvature bounded below, to the setting of Busemann spaces with non-negative curvature. We prove that any finite-dimensional Busemann space with non-negative curvature, satisfying Ohta's $S$-concavity and local semi-convexity, admits a non-trivial Hausdorff measure of integer dimension, satisfies the measure contraction property and contains an open dense topological manifold part with full measure. We also show that such spaces are rectifiable and almost every point admits a unique tangent cone isometric to a finite-dimensional Banach space. Finally, based on a refined analysis on strainers and asymmetric angles, we obtain a Hausdorff dimension estimate for singular strata, and show that such spaces admit a natural measure-theoretic stratification. Our results enrich the theory of synthetic sectional curvature lower bounds for metric spaces, and provide some useful tools and examples to study Finslerian metric measure spaces.
item.dc:creator: Bang-Xian Han, Liming Yin

item.title: A minimal regularity for the area formula in the Engel group
item.description: arXiv:2602.00346v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove that the upper blow-up theorem in the Engel group holds for $C^1$ submanifolds. Combining this result with the known negligibility of the singular set, we obtain an integral representation of the spherical measure for all surfaces of class $C^{1,\alpha}$ in the Engel group. A new and central aspect of our method is the suitable use of Stokes' theorem to prove the upper blow-up, which relies on the special algebraic structure of left-invariant forms in the Engel group. Some general tools are also introduced to establish area formulas in arbitrary stratified group.
item.dc:creator: Francesca Corni, Fares Essebei, Valentino Magnani

item.title: Simultaneous random polytope approximation characterizes the Euclidean ball
item.description: arXiv:2602.18547v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this work, we present a new geometric characterization of the Euclidean ball based on approximation by random polytopes. We investigate when a single boundary sampling density is asymptotically optimal for two random polytope approximation problems, and show that for a convex body in $\R^d$ with $C^2$ boundary and everywhere positive principal curvatures, one fixed density minimizes the leading expected errors for any two distinct intrinsic volume differences of inscribed random polytopes if and only if the body is a Euclidean ball. We show that an analogous characterization holds for the volume and mean width differences of circumscribed random polytopes, and that uniform sampling gives the converse statement in both models. We also determine the unique density minimizing the average of two normalized leading errors, and obtain an explicit positive gap for every nonball. The proofs combine classical random polytope asymptotics, H\"older's inequality, and a curvature rigidity argument based on the Hsiung--Minkowski identities and Newton--Maclaurin inequalities.
item.dc:creator: Steven Hoehner

item.title: The Five Distance Theorem For An Arbitrary Norm
item.description: arXiv:2608.12405v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The three gap theorem states that the points of the Kronecker sequence $\alpha,2\alpha,\ldots,N\alpha$, considered modulo one, divide the circle into intervals of at most three distinct lengths. In a two-dimensional nearest-neighbour analogue, Haynes and Marklof proved that the Kronecker sequence modulo an arbitrary unimodular lattice determines at most five distinct nearest-neighbour distances in the Euclidean norm, and that this bound is sharp. Dettmann subsequently constructed examples attaining five distinct distances for every $\ell_p$-norm, $1\leq p\leq\infty$. We prove the corresponding upper bound for every norm on $\mathbb R^2$: for every full-rank lattice $L$, every $\alpha\in\mathbb R^2$, and every $N\in\mathbb N$, the number of distinct nearest-neighbour distances is at most five. For every norm, this bound is attained for some $L$ and $\alpha$. For strictly convex norms, the proof extends the lattice-theoretic argument of Haynes and Marklof by replacing the Euclidean angular estimates with a cone lemma based on a proper Brass angular measure. The result for arbitrary norms is then obtained by a strictly convex perturbation and a limiting argument.
item.dc:creator: Nikita A. Mironov, Oleg R. Musin

item.title: On the monotonicity of magnitude functions of negative type finite semimetric spaces
item.description: arXiv:2608.15720v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Motivated by the conjectured monotonicity of the magnitude functions of metric spaces of negative type, we investigate the monotonicity problem for finite semimetric spaces, namely, ``metric spaces without the triangle inequality''. We completely resolve this problem by proving that the monotonicity holds for negative type semimetric spaces with at most three points, while constructing negative type semimetric spaces with at least four points whose magnitude functions are not monotonically increasing. We also prove monotonicity for all 4-point metric spaces and construct 12-point metric spaces of negative type whose magnitude functions are not monotonically increasing.
item.dc:creator: Kiyonori Gomi, Hiroshi Tsuji

item.title: The isoperimetric problem for four-dimensional parallelohedra
item.description: arXiv:2610.01653v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The honeycomb and Kelvin problems ask how space can be partitioned into cells of equal volume with the least surface area. We resolve this question in four dimensions for convex bodies that tile space by translations, showing that the regular $24$-cell uniquely minimizes surface area at fixed volume. We develop a framework combining an exact deficit identity, valid in every dimension, with a descent argument. As a consequence, the regular $24$-cell also minimizes surface area among such tiles containing a fixed ball.
item.dc:creator: Matteo Novaga, Lark Song

item.title: Higher-order Godbersen inequality and a characterization of simplices via the face lattice
item.description: arXiv:2610.06806v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We settle the long-standing Godbersen conjecture that the mixed volume of a convex body of fixed positive volume with its reflection about the origin is maximized precisely by simplices. For the proof, we establish a new characterization of simplices by a natural incidence relation on the face lattice. Moreover, we establish a higher-order generalization of the Godbersen inequality and show that simplices are the only nontrivial equality cases, confirming a conjecture of Schneider from 2000.
item.dc:creator: Filip Fry\v{s}, Jan Kotrbat\'y, Mohamed A. Mouamine, Shouda Wang

item.title: Symmetric products and finite subset spaces of absolute Lipschitz retracts
item.description: arXiv:2610.10976v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove that the $Q$th symmetric product of an absolute $\lambda$-Lipschitz retract, equipped with the bottleneck matching metric, is an absolute $(3Q-2)\lambda$-Lipschitz retract. This answers a question of De Pauw about the target spaces of Almgren's $Q$-valued maps. We also prove that the space of nonempty subsets with at most $n$ points, equipped with the Hausdorff metric, is an absolute $(6n-5)\lambda$-Lipschitz retract. The main tool is a reconstruction theorem for bounded products of metric stars with finitely many rays, modulo a finite permutation group: these quotients are absolute $3$-Lipschitz retracts, independently of the group and the number of coordinates. A variant of this theorem, in which unordered sets of sign vectors take the place of the group action, handles finite subset spaces.
item.dc:creator: Leonid V. Kovalev

item.title: Sharp Minimax Gram-Determinant Asymptotics for Labelled Unit Decompositions of the Identity and Recent Developments on Makai's Conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2610.10979v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We show that Gonz\'alez Merino and Schymura's Conjecture 4.8, a sufficient condition for Makai's reverse isodiametric conjecture, fails in all sufficiently large dimensions. Its three-dimensional case follows from Aliev's proof. Pe{\l}czy\'nski and Szarek's construction for enclosing parallelepipeds implies this failure. Using random frames, we also determine the sharp exponential determinant guarantee for every fixed ratio greater than one between the number of vectors and the dimension.
item.dc:creator: Haozhou Zhang

item.title: A fixed point theorem for the action of linear higher rank algebraic groups over local fields on symmetric spaces of infinite dimension and finite rank
item.description: arXiv:2505.05220v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let F be a non-archimedean local field of characteristic zero whose residue field has at least three elements. Let G be an almost simple linear algebraic group over F, with rank_F(G) >= 2. Let X be a simply connected symmetric space of infinite dimension and finite rank, with non-positive curvature operator. We prove that every continuous action by isometries of G on X has a fixed point. If the group G contains SL_3(F), the result holds without any assumption on the non-archimedean local field F. The result extends to cocompact lattices in G if the cardinality of the residue field of F is large enough, with a bound that depends on rank_F(G).
item.arxiv:journal_reference: International Mathematics Research Notices, Volume 2026, Issue 20, October 2026, rnag229
item.dc:creator: Federico Viola

item.title: On exponential separation of analytic self-conformal sets on the real line
item.description: arXiv:2509.07888v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In a recent article, Rapaport showed that there is no dimension drop for exponentially separated analytic IFSs on the real line. We show that the set of such exponentially separated IFSs in the space of analytic IFSs contains an open and dense set in the $\mathcal{C}^2$ topology. Moreover, we give a sufficient condition for the IFS to be exponentially separated which allows us to construct explicit examples which are exponentially separated. The key technical tool is the introduction of the \emph{dual IFS} which we believe has significant interest in its own right. As an application we also characterise when an analytic IFS can be conjugated to a self-similar IFS.
item.dc:creator: Bal\'azs B\'ar\'any, Istv\'an Kolossv\'ary, Sascha Troscheit

item.title: Remarks on a result of Sibony on the Carath\'eodory topology
item.description: arXiv:2512.03901v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this paper, we prove that if a Carath\'eodory hyperbolic analytic space $X$ is $C_X$-complete, then its natural topology is induced by the Carath\'eodory distance on $X$. This is an improvement of Sibony's result, which concludes the same under the hypothesis that $X$ is $C_X$-finitely compact. This improvement is not merely formal; we also show the existence of uncountably many biholomorphically inequivalent analytic spaces that are not $C_X$-finitely compact but are $C_X$-complete.
item.dc:creator: Sudip Dolai

item.title: Random Polyhedral Cones I: Distributional Results via Gale Duality
item.description: arXiv:2602.08581v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $U_1,\ldots,U_n$ be independent random vectors uniformly distributed on the unit sphere $\mathbb S^{d-1}\subseteq\mathbb R^d$, where $n\ge d$, and consider the random polyhedral cone \[ \mathcal W_{n,d}:=\mathop{\mathrm{pos}} (U_1,\ldots,U_n) = \{\lambda_1 U_1+ \ldots + \lambda_n U_n: \lambda_1\geq 0, \ldots, \lambda_n \geq 0\}. \] We establish several distributional results for $\mathcal W_{n,d}$ and the associated spherical polytope $\mathcal W_{n,d}\cap\mathbb S^{d-1}$. Our main contributions include: (i) Let $\alpha_d$ denote the solid angle of $\mathcal W_{d,d}$ and write $m(d,k):=\mathbb E[\alpha_d^k]$ for its $k$-th moment. We prove the symmetry $m(d,k)=m(k,d)$. As an application, we compute $\mathop{\mathrm{Var}}[\alpha_d]=2^{-d}(d+1)^{-1}-4^{-d}$ and derive a closed formula for the third moment. (ii) For $n=d+1,d+2,d+3$ we determine the probability that $\mathcal W_{n,d}\cap\mathbb S^{d-1}$ is a spherical simplex, a spherical analogue of the classical Sylvester problem. In the case $n=d+2$ we also determine the distribution of the number of vertices of $\mathcal W_{d+2,d}\cap\mathbb S^{d-1}$. (iii) Let $f_\ell(\mathcal W_{n,d})$ denote the number of $\ell$-dimensional faces of $\mathcal W_{n,d}$. We prove a distributional limit theorem for $f_\ell(\mathcal W_{n,d})$ in the regime $n=d+k$ and $\ell=d-q$, where $k,q\in\mathbb N$ are fixed and $d\to\infty$. The limit law is a weighted sum of independent chi squared variables, with weights given by explicit eigenvalues of a convolution operator on the sphere. A unifying ingredient is an explicit coupling producing i.i.d. uniform vectors $U_1,\ldots,U_n\in\mathbb S^{d-1}$ together with i.i.d. uniform vectors $V_1,\ldots,V_n\in\mathbb S^{n-d-1}$ whose associated oriented matroids are Gale dual.
item.dc:creator: Zakhar Kabluchko

item.title: Nonlinear Lebesgue spaces: Curves and geometry
item.description: arXiv:2603.09459v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: This paper is the second in a series by the author and collaborators devoted to the study of geometric and analytic properties of nonlinear Lebesgue spaces, that is, L^p spaces of mappings taking values in arbitrary metric spaces. The present article formalizes the pointwise description of their geometric properties---their length structure, bounds on their Alexandrov curvature as well as the definition of a velocity for absolutely continuous curves despite the lack of differential structure. To obtain this pointwise description, we first prove a nonlinear analogue of the Fubini--Lebesgue theorem, which yields an identification of L^p curves in nonlinear Lebesgue spaces with mappings taking values in the space of L^p curves. This identification of L^p curves then enables a similar identification for absolutely continuous curves, from which the pointwise description of the geometric properties of nonlinear Lebesgue spaces follows.
item.dc:creator: Guillaume S\'erieys (MAP5 - UMR 8145)

item.title: Fourier analytic variants of the Furstenberg and Kakeya problems
item.description: arXiv:2605.21668v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study several distinct but related Fourier analytic variants of the well-known Kakeya and Furstenberg set problems in the plane. For example, given $0<s,t<1$, we call a set $K \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$ an $(s,t)$-Kakeya set if there exists a set of directions $E \subseteq S^1$ with Hausdorff dimension at least $t$ such that, for each $e \in E$, the set $K$ contains a subset of a unit line segment in direction $e$ whose Fourier dimension, viewed as a subset of $\mathbb{R}$, is at least $s$. For $\Delta(s,t)$ defined to be the infimum of the Fourier dimension among all $(s,t)$-Kakeya sets in $\mathbb{R}^2$, we prove that \[ \Delta(s,t) = \min\{s,2t\}. \] We also obtain similar results in the Furstenberg set version of the problem and in the case where the Hausdorff dimension of the collection of lines is replaced by the Fourier dimension.
item.dc:creator: Jonathan M. Fraser, Lijian Yang

item.title: Graphon as a Bridge between Graphs and Manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2607.20213v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We show that there exist graphons that interpolate between Riemannian manifolds and weighted geometric graphs. Specifically, the graph-to-manifold approximation used in manifold learning can be regarded as the composition of a graph-to-graphon convergence and a graphon-to-manifold convergence in a certain sense. Furthermore, we establish a monotonicity inequality which reveals an implicit relationship between numerous combinatorial parameters and geometric quantities on graphons. Using this inequality, we find relations among conductance, maxcut problem, capacity, and packing radius, as well as their limiting behaviors under graph-to-graphon and graphon-to-manifold convergences; some of these relations are novel even for simple graphs and closed manifolds. We also find that in the graphon-to-manifold limiting process, the purely combinatorial parameters diverge, leading to a ``blowup'' phenomenon; and continuous versions of some graph parameters cannot be realized via Riemannian manifolds, but can be realized via graphons.

item.title: Maximal volume of convex bodies avoiding random points and lacunary dilates
item.description: arXiv:2610.09790v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: For a positive real lacunary sequence and any probability measure $\mu$ with polynomial Fourier decay, we determine, for $\mu$-almost every $x$, the asymptotic maximal volume of convex bodies avoiding the first $N$ dilates of $x$ modulo $\mathbb Z^d$. Among homothets of a fixed convex body, the maximal volume is asymptotic to $(\log N)/N$. When all convex bodies in the unit cube are allowed, it is asymptotic to $d(\log N)/N$. For independent uniform points in a fixed convex body $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^d$, the maximal volume of an empty convex body is asymptotic to $d\operatorname{vol}(\Omega)(\log N)/N$ almost surely. We also show, by constructing a one-dimensional counterexample, that lacunarity cannot be replaced by sparsity on sublacunary scales.
